purpose: Adjudicate a representative cross-section of the exact-upstream marketing catalog while separating repository-level executable surface, Skill-level payload closure, persistent context, recurring automation, outbound communication, and ordinary instruction-only methods.

cohort.selectionBasis: Representative instruction-only writing and research methods plus cross-source collision, persistent-context, recurring-scheduler, repository-dependency, outbound-compliance, and persona-simulation counterexamples.
cohort.interpretation: Repository-level scripts and integration CLIs raise source-level review cost, but they are not attributed to a selected Skill unless that Skill references or packages them. Conversely, an instruction-only Skill may still depend on repository-level tools, accounts, data, scheduling, or persistent files.

representativeSkills.name: copywriting
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: Instruction and reference material only; claims, testimonials, customer language, source text, and publication remain task-bound and must not be invented or published without authorization.
representativeSkills.distinctCoverage: Marketing-page structure, evidence checks, CTA alternatives, and conversion-copy annotations.
representativeSkills.reason: Dependency-complete and low executable surface, with enough domain-specific structure to justify a bounded comparison rather than immediate duplication.

representativeSkills.name: copy-editing
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: Edits user-bound copy only; the optional simulated expert-panel scoring is heuristic review, not independent expert evidence or publication acceptance.
representativeSkills.distinctCoverage: Seven focused editing sweeps with explicit intent-preservation and proof checks.
representativeSkills.reason: Dependency-complete and method-specific, but overlap and the value of its simulated scoring gate require an outcome comparison.

representativeSkills.name: customer-research
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: May process transcripts, surveys, support tickets, reviews, participant language, and public online sources. Each task must bind provenance, privacy, consent, retention, access, quotation, and external-research authority.
representativeSkills.distinctCoverage: Confidence-labeled voice-of-customer synthesis, source-bias checks, proxy-persona limits, and research-gap outputs.
representativeSkills.reason: Dependency-complete and includes useful anti-invention guardrails, but task-time data and browsing boundaries plus overlap require controlled comparison.

representativeSkills.name: marketing-ideas
representativeSkills.collision: Exact declared name also exists in the pinned phuryn/pm-skills source.
representativeSkills.reason: A manager route cannot safely admit two exact-name candidates without a one-route, composition, precedence, and attribution decision based on behavior rather than catalog size.

representativeSkills.name: product-marketing
representativeSkills.crossSkillClaim: All other marketing Skills read this shared context automatically.
representativeSkills.distinctCoverage: Versioned product-positioning context with an append-only changelog for downstream marketing work.
representativeSkills.reason: The continuity idea is relevant, but a third-party Skill cannot unilaterally claim the shared .agents namespace, move legacy files, or establish a cross-Skill authority source without a portable adapter, destination ownership, and write authorization.

representativeSkills.name: marketing-loops
representativeSkills.reason: The guardrail model is useful architecture input, but recurring activation, host scheduling, state storage, resource use, and downstream Skill availability cannot be admitted as one portable Skill route.

representativeSkills.name: analytics
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: Analytics account creation, tag changes, tracking code, consent mode, user identifiers, retention, and production verification are separate account, code, privacy, and deployment transitions.
representativeSkills.reason: Selective Skill installation would preserve local references but break the declared repository-level tools registry and integration guides; privacy and account changes also require task-bound review.

representativeSkills.name: cold-email
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: Drafting is separable from prospect-data acquisition, personalization research, account access, sending, cadence execution, suppression handling, jurisdictional compliance, and recipient consent or legitimate-interest assessment.
riskSignals: no explicit compliance front gate in the Skill body
representativeSkills.reason: Instruction-only drafting does not itself send messages, but broad invocation without a compliance and data front gate could normalize unsolicited multi-touch outreach.

representativeSkills.name: marketing-council
representativeSkills.permissionAndDataBoundary: Optional live research must remain source-, cost-, recency-, and citation-bound; simulated living-person views are not real endorsement or independent expert review.
representativeSkills.reason: Its grounding rules are useful design input, but persona simulation plus heavy overlap does not yet outperform direct evidence-grounded premise challenge or justify another active route.

portfolioOverlapSnapshot.snapshotMeaning: Current route visibility and names are comparison inputs only, not live loading, behavior, value, or redundancy proof.

managerBoundary.nextSafeAction: Keep the source inactive; compare the three low-executable candidates against current routes, and separately design portable adapters for persistent context and recurring lifecycle before any manager registration or install request.
